title: Al-Mu'akhkhir, the Delayer
hookLine: the Delayer, who puts back in wisdom
tomorrow: before the first word of anything, what do Muslims say?

cards: Delayed in transit. A new departure time in orange letters on the board. Delivered, not read.
Yesterday's question was what happens when He puts something back, and today's Name is exactly that: Al-Mu'akhkhir, the Delayer, the one who puts back. It's a hard Name to love on a waiting day.
So one question for today: is a delay a no?

teach.b: Islam's answer starts with the pair. In the Prophet's du'a, the two Names stand together: the one who brings forward, the one who puts back. Same hand, same wisdom.

teach.h: YE HATE A THING WHICH IS GOOD.
teach.b: The Qur'an says it plainly, in Pickthall's words: "it may happen that ye hate a thing which is good for you," and it ends, "Allah knoweth, ye know not."

And in Sahih al-Bukhari the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says a person's du'a is answered as long as they don't grow impatient and say, I prayed, and nothing came. So in this picture, put back is not thrown out.
Now a neighbor says something close.

teach.h: A NEIGHBOR: A TIME FOR EVERY PURPOSE.
teach.b: In the Bible, Ecclesiastes, read by Jews and Christians alike, opens a well-known chapter: "To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven."
A time to plant, it goes on, and a time to pluck up. What's shared is real: time isn't ours to run, and things have their hour. And here's the honest difference, ranking no one.

Ecclesiastes lists the seasons, and keeps admitting that no one can find out God's work from beginning to end. Islam takes the delay itself and gives it a Name of God, one you can call on in a du'a, ya Mu'akhkhir.

teach.h: ONE NAMES THE SEASONS, ONE THE SETTER.

teach.b: The other names the One who sets them.

how: Muslims facing a delay may recall 2:216 and keep making du'a; the paired Names al-Muqaddim and al-Mu'akhkhir are said together in a du'a of the Prophet.

o: the one who forgets a request for a time
the one who puts things back, in wisdom
the one who punishes by making you wait

games.q: who says what about time — tap the pairs.
p: you may hate what is good for you
to every thing there is a season

s: a delayed du'a is a refused du'a
in Bukhari, a du'a is answered as long as you don't give up saying 'i prayed, and nothing came.'
Al-Mu'akhkhir is paired with Al-Muqaddim in the Prophet's du'a
the one who brings forward and the one who puts back, side by side.
'to every thing there is a season' is a line from the Qur'an
it's Ecclesiastes 3:1, in the Bible. the Qur'an says something close in its own way.

games.q: your cousin's visa is delayed and the wedding has to move. your aunt says, 'it's a sign it was never meant to be.' what does today's Name say?
o: put back isn't thrown out; the Delayer puts things back in wisdom.
she's right: when God delays something, that's His way of saying no.
it's only paperwork; timing has nothing to do with God at all.
games.why: in the Prophet's du'a the one who puts back stands beside the one who brings forward. a delay, in this picture, is a shelf, not a trash can.

practice: Close your eyes and name one thing that's on hold: a reply, a result, a healing. Don't push it forward and don't throw it away. For the sit, just set it down on a shelf in your mind, put back, not lost.

wordCard.voice: Al-Mu'akhkhir. The Delayer: the one who puts back in wisdom, named right beside the one who brings forward.

orig.note: Arabic: the Delayer, the one who puts back. it's paired with al-Muqaddim.

carryVoice: Carry this: put back, on a shelf you can't see from here. Name seventy-two, and the week nearly done.
